coursesReviewed.name: Personal & Professional Development
coursesReviewed.finding: Mandatory Year1 personal and academic formation; not a substitute for legal-academic skills.

coursesReviewed.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: reading financial statements supports analysis of the economic position of businesses and the commercial relationships studied in the law/business strand.

coursesReviewed.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: AI bias, privacy, fairness, corporate governance and regulation provide a concrete contemporary application of commercial and social responsibility.

coursesReviewed.name: Transnational Business Law
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: legal frameworks for cross-border contracts, trade, intellectual property, foreign investment and digital commerce, applied through problem-based work and arbitration simulation.

coursesReviewed.name: Money, Banking & Finance
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: financial data, risk and investment/budget decisions explain the economic interests in commercial relationships; this is not a banking-law course.

coursesReviewed.name: Introduction to Economics
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: incentives, markets, firms and public intervention support the target’s explicit study of the social-economic function of law.

coursesReviewed.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: strategic behaviour, imperfect competition, externalities and efficiency support analysis of how rules affect economic relationships; not competition-law doctrine.

coursesReviewed.name: Public Economics
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: taxation, redistribution, externalities and public spending support analysis of public institutions and legal policy; not fiscal-law doctrine.

coursesReviewed.name: Econometrics
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary method: OLS, GLS and instrumental variables support empirical analysis of economic relationships, including the target’s law-in-action questions; not doctrinal legal research.

coursesReviewed.name: Strategy & Digital Transformation
coursesReviewed.finding: Removed: preparing a digital-transformation strategy does not supply sufficient legal inquiry.

coursesReviewed.name: Market Research
coursesReviewed.finding: Removed: customer-market research is not the target’s empirical legal research.

coursesReviewed.name: International Business & Governance
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: cross-border governance, corporate responsibility and global trade analyse the institutional setting of international commercial relationships.

coursesReviewed.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: experiential venture development exposes the commercial organisations and transactions examined in transnational business law and supplies its formal prerequisite; it does not teach law.

coursesReviewed.name: Research Methods & Statistics
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary method: research design, sampling, experiments, surveys and statistics support empirical law-in-action inquiry; group research is not a law thesis.

coursesReviewed.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
coursesReviewed.finding: Removed: organisational psychology is adjacent; the final business programme is strengthened by actual criminal-law reasoning.

coursesReviewed.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary skill: principled negotiation, objective criteria and simulations support conflict resolution and reasoned argument; not a legal procedure or moot-court course.

coursesReviewed.name: Law, Society & Justice
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: legal systems, sources and selected public/private fields are studied through legal, social and normative perspectives, case law and trial simulations.

coursesReviewed.name: Modern History
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: sovereignty, national self-determination, welfare states, decolonisation and European cooperation supply specific historical foundations for public authority.

coursesReviewed.name: History of Empires
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: imperial power, theories of empire and great-power politics support the historical interpretation of international orders; not public international-law doctrine.

coursesReviewed.name: Western Way of War
coursesReviewed.finding: Removed: military history is too indirect for the proposed public-law programme when more specific legal/normative study is available.

coursesReviewed.name: History Research Seminar
coursesReviewed.finding: Removed: a primary-source project on the1809WalcherenExpedition is not legal-academic research and has insufficient specific weight in these law concepts.

coursesReviewed.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: positive human-rights law, treaties, monitoring and case law are integrated with historical and philosophical arguments about rights.

coursesReviewed.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: accountability, guilt, legality, punishment, case analysis and a legal-aid simulation implement substantive criminal reasoning; no dedicated Dutch criminal-procedure sequence.

coursesReviewed.name: Introduction to Public International Law
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: sources and subjects of international law, force, armed conflict, international crime, refugees, environmental law and treaty politics; coverage is not identical to the Erasmus syllabus.

coursesReviewed.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: comparative constitutional and administrative principles, government powers and civil liberties; not advanced Dutch administrative procedure.

coursesReviewed.name: Principles of Private Law
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: comparative property, tort and contract principles in five legal systems; no dedicated Dutch obligations, insolvency or civil-procedure sequence.

coursesReviewed.name: Foundations of European Union Law
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct: EU institutions, legal foundations, fundamental rights, citizenship, free movement and domestic effects, using procedural work and substantive PBL cases.

coursesReviewed.name: Ethics
coursesReviewed.finding: Direct normative contribution: virtue ethics, deontology and utilitarianism support the target’s legal-philosophy themes; practical ethics is not a complete legal-philosophy syllabus.

coursesReviewed.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: justification of political power and comparison of classical and contemporary political arguments support normative study of public authority.

coursesReviewed.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: democratisation, state institutions, courts and the interaction of state and society support empirical analysis of constitutional government.

coursesReviewed.name: Theory of International Relations
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: competing international-relations theories and a Security Council simulation support analysis of the political operation of international orders.

coursesReviewed.name: European Union Politics
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: EU actors, decision rules and research on interest groups and legislative dossiers explain the political operation of EU law and public authority.

coursesReviewed.name: Peace & Conflict
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: theories of conflict, justice and reconciliation connect public authority, civil society and international institutional responses; not legal doctrine.

coursesReviewed.name: Introduction to Sociology
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: social institutions, inequality and sociological theory support the target’s explicit law/society and empirical-law foundations.

coursesReviewed.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary method: qualitative design, data collection, interpretation and reflexivity support empirical investigation of law’s social operation.

coursesReviewed.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: social-movement theory and environmental-justice cases explain how civic groups formulate justice claims and contest public decisions.

coursesReviewed.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary: civil society, public spheres, trust and empirical work with civic organisations support analysis of institutions and law’s social setting.

coursesReviewed.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary skill: rhetorical analysis, academic essays and oral arguments support reasoned communication; not legal drafting or doctrinal research.

coursesReviewed.name: Persuasive Communication
coursesReviewed.finding: Complementary skill: framing, persuasion ethics and applied institutional communication support public/legal argument; not the Erasmus legal moot court.

unusedCandidate: Rhetoric in Action was inspected and rejected: its project teaches primary-school pupils, so generic rhetorical-skill relevance alone does not justify adding it to these law programmes.
comparability: The final pass tested the strongest competing explanation: that coherent political or business programmes disguise the absence of substantive law. Options 1 and 3 each contain eight actual law/rights courses (60 EC); option 2 contains five (37.5 EC), supported by normative and public-institutional inquiry. These courses directly study legal systems, sources, rights, constitutional powers, private/criminal reasoning and European/international law. Their complementary fields support specific questions evidenced by the broad Law target. This is sufficient for qualified related-field comparisons, while the missing depth in Dutch doctrine, procedure and legal research remains explicit. Course counts are descriptive evidence, not a numerical comparability threshold.
